locales.description: This post names a public political figure — such as a politician, candidate, judge, senior appointed or party official, political operative, prominent political activist, or prominent political media figure — matched against a public, published gazetteer. It is a factual tag about who is named, not a judgment about whether the post is political discourse. Applied per post, never per account. Ambiguous names only receive this label when the public-figure reading is corroborated. It never infers the author's affiliation, ideology, or intent.
locales.name: Names a political figure

locales.description: This post overtly discusses politics: it uses unambiguous political terminology (elections, legislation, parties, policy debate, political office) or names political figures in a political context, with enough corroborating signals to be confident. Determinations are made by published, deterministic rules — the term lists, weights, and thresholds are public in the project repository, and any labeling decision is reproducible from the post's text alone. Applied per post, never per account; it describes the post's topic only, not the author's affiliation, ideology, or intent. When in doubt, no label is applied.
locales.name: Political

locales.description: This post discusses a politicized topic (for example immigration, abortion, tariffs, or gun policy) or plausibly references political actors or events without overt markers. It is a lower-confidence, opt-in tier — off by default; you see it only if you enable it in this labeler's settings. All inference lives here rather than in the confident tiers. Like the others it is applied per post, never per account, and describes the post's topic only, not the author's affiliation, ideology, or intent.
locales.name: Likely political
